subject: Dedicated sizing: traffic trajectory + burst scenarios intake
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@quantaflow.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing: traffic trajectory + burst scenarios intake

Hi Elaine,

Thanks for the call earlier — great to hear how Quantaflow is planning for holiday surge and the upcoming API expansion. To scope a Dedicated commitment and propose a GPU mix, we need a concise traffic trajectory + burst scenario breakdown from your telemetry. I attached a short template (redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx) — filling the shaded fields will get us to a preliminary fleet sketch.

Top things that move sizing:
- Peak 5-minute concurrency (and the 95/99 percentiles over a rolling 24h)
- Typical prompt length distribution (tokens): median / p75 / p95 / p99
- Typical response length distribution (tokens) and whether response truncation is acceptable
- Ratio of chat like, single-turn generate, and embeddings calls (percent)
- Burst shape examples: short spikes (1–5 minutes), medium (10–30 minutes), and long (hour+ sustained) — please annotate historical dates if available
- Any customer-level fanout (single user -> N downstream calls) or amplification patterns

If you can drop the template back by EOD tomorrow we’ll turn this into a capacity sketch and a couple of price scenarios (reserved+burst vs. reserved+on-demand fallback). Also please attach a representative token histogram export if you have one — we can use that to validate batching assumptions.

Quick ask: is Quantaflow okay with a short controlled load-run (10–15 minutes) on a non-prod key to validate peak occupancy estimates? That helps us verify KV cache effectiveness for your prompt shapes.

Thanks,
Soojin
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx (spreadsheet; template with shaded fields)

From: Elaine Park <elaine@quantaflow.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@quantaflow.ai
Date: 2026-11-28T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing: traffic trajectory + burst scenarios intake

Hi Soojin — thanks, appreciate the clear list. We filled the template and attaching a short token histogram. Highlights below (pulled from Nov production window):

- Peak 5-min concurrency: 1,420 (observed on 2026-11-24 17:05 PST), rolling p95: 1,180, p99: 1,390
- Typical request mix: chat 62%, single-turn generate 28%, embeddings 10%
- Prompt length tokens (median/p75/p95/p99): 48 / 110 / 420 / 1,800
- Response length tokens (median/p75/p95/p99): 64 / 210 / 950 / 2,400 (we truncate at 4k tokens currently)
- Burst shapes: short spikes (1–5m) ~45% of incidents; medium (10–30m) ~40%; long (>1h) ~15%
- Fanout: about 8% of sessions fan out to 3+ backend calls (webhook + summarization + store)

We attached qf_token_histogram.csv (samples for the busiest day), and the completed XLSX template.

On the load-run: yes, we can approve a short controlled run on a staging API key — I’ll loop ops if you confirm exact time and concurrency target.

—Elaine
VP Product
Quantaflow

Attachments: qf_token_histogram.csv, filled-redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@quantaflow.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T13:26:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing: traffic trajectory + burst scenarios intake

Great — this is exactly what we needed, thanks. A few clarifying points before we produce a compact fleet sketch: 

1) The p99 prompt length (1,800 tokens) — is that driven by a small number of long-document batch uploads, or is it live interactive typing? If batch uploads, can you share whether those calls are predominantly single-turn generate or embeddings?

2) For the 8% fanout sessions, are the downstream calls synchronous (blocking) or fired-and-forget? If synchronized, they multiply concurrency for the end-to-end flow — we model that differently.

3) For the load-run window — propose Tue 2026-12-01 09:00–09:15 PT with a 1,600 concurrency target and short ramp (30s). Ops, please confirm.

We’ll produce two preliminary fleet sketches:
- Conservatively sized reserved fleet with a conservative occupancy target (60%); plus on-demand fallback for heavy tail
- Aggressively sized reserved fleet (75% occupancy) with a small buffer of burst-capacity we can gate

Sending to Marissa to include pricing options and a rough timeline to commit.

—Soojin

Hi Elaine — quick confirmation from infra side: we can run the proposed 15-minute staging load-run at Tue 2026-12-01 09:00 PT targeting 1,600 concurrency. A couple of operational notes:

- We’ll instrument KV-cache hit rate and occupancy during the run; please set a low-priority staging key so we can safely throttle if downstream systems backpressure.
- For sizing sketches, we assume with your prompt/response mix the A800 mix yields ~18–22% better token throughput vs baseline A100; quantization to 4-bit is acceptable on the higher-latency tails but we need confirmation for any strict quality gates.

Elaine — if that looks good we’ll proceed and Marissa will share the pricing sketches today.
